thread.title: Will Foray Into Bitcoin Factor Into Future Earnings Growth At Square?

author: Investor's Business Daily
title: Will Foray Into Bitcoin Factor Into Future Earnings Growth At Square?
text:
Shutterstock photo
It's not the first stock you think of when it comes to Bitcoin, but Square ( SQ ) has jumped onto the cryptocurrency bandwagon.
[ibd-display-video id=2382612 width=50 float=left autostart=true] In November, the digital payment processor announced that users of its Square Cash money-transfer service added a Bitcoin cryptocurrency buying option. Square Cash lets users send money via email and competes with similar services from PayPal ( PYPL ) and Apple ( AAPL ).
The company hasn't mentioned much about the new service, but its stock has already felt the consequences of being part of the volatile cryptocurrency market.
Square shares plunged 16% on Nov. 27, when a BTIG analyst downgraded the stock to sell from neutral, saying the stock's rally was overdone amid the Bitcoin buzz.
"We believe (Square's) valuation already reflects emphatic and unimpeded growth while failing to factor in competitive, credit-related and macro risks that did not go away when some investors suddenly viewed its shares as a play on a trendy cryptocurrency," the BTIG report noted.
Square is best known for credit-card readers that plug into mobile phones and tablets. That makes Square a popular option with merchants who sell on the go, although it also provides point-of-sale terminals for store operators. Payroll, billing, analytics and other services for sellers are offered as well.
As it recovers from the downgrade-related sell-off, Square is forming the right side of a cup-shaped base . The potential buy point is 49.66. A breakout could extend a nearly yearlong advance for Square.
Since the stock broke out to new highs in February 2017, shares have more than tripled in value. Most growth stocks are in late-stage bases by the time they've tripled, and Square is technically in a third-stage base, where risk is higher. The sheer size of its yearlong rally is enough to make shrewd investors pause and carefully consider whether Square is capable of another long run.
A member of IBD's Stock Spotlight screen, the company has good profit and sales growth to justify a new advance. Earnings increased 250% and 600% the past two quarters, albeit from tiny single-digit EPS comparisons. In the first quarter of 2017, Square posted a profit of 5 cents a share vs. a net loss of 5 cents a year earlier.
The three-year average sales growth rate is a solid 55%, and growth in the top line has accelerated the past couple of quarters.
Analysts expect Q4 sales of $266.3 million and earnings of 7 cents a share, vs. 5 cents in the year-ago period. The company made its first profit in 2016.
An A- Accumulation/Distribution Rating in IBD Stock Checkup says institutional investors remain interested in Square.
